claims.explanation: TWS-119 is a GSK3 inhibitor that activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling; selectivity likely reflects dependence on Wnt/β-catenin-driven transcriptional programs, with sensitizing features being mutations that activate the pathway (APC, CTNNB1, RNF43) or high β-catenin/TCF activity, and protective features being intact GSK3-dependent or low-Wnt states. The observed enrichment of TP53 mutations and BRAF/PIK3CA alterations in sensitive lines is consistent with these pathways cooperating with Wnt activation, while PTEN loss and NF1 mutations in resistant lines suggest PI3K/MAPK-driven bypass. Direct evidence for GSK3β/Wnt involvement comes from PMID 38041178, which used TWS-119 to activate Wnt signaling in CRC models.

features.basis: Activating β-catenin mutations mimic GSK3 inhibition and predict Wnt-pathway dependence
APC loss activates β-catenin; sensitive CRC lines SNUC5 and HEC265 carry APC/CTNNB1 alterations
RNF43 loss stabilizes Wnt receptors and increases β-catenin signaling
AXIN1 loss impairs β-catenin destruction complex, mimicking GSK3 inhibition
BRAF-mutant lines (SNUC5, IGR37, K029AX, HEC265) are enriched among sensitive lines
PIK3CA-mutant lines (SNUC5, SNU840, KYSE510) appear among sensitive lines
TP53 mutations are nearly universal in sensitive lines, though common overall
PTEN loss is enriched in resistant lines (ZR751, FTC133, KALS1, UACC62, 786O)
NF1 mutations appear in resistant lines (FTC133, KALS1, LOXIMVI, BICR6, S117)
TWS-119 downregulates MYC in the virtual cell; high MYC may buffer GSK3 inhibition
TWS-119 downregulates CCND1 in the virtual cell; cyclin D1-high lines may resist
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) are among sensitive lines
